body:
I don't think this change is correct. The C# types are just converting the `Variant` elements to `T` every time an element is added/removed/accessed from the collection, the underlying type stored is still `Variant`.

To be clear about what the documentation was saying:

> Typed wrapper around Godot's Array class, an array of Variant typed elements allocated in the engine in C+++.

This is describing the native C++ `Array` type that the C# type is a wrapper of. Even when the array is typed, the underlying storage is still `Variant` (`TypedArray<int32_t>` stores the `int32_t` elements as `Variant`).

This is different from packed arrays that actually store the element they are specifically designed to hold. For example, a `PackedByteArray` stores the elements as `byte`. As a result `PackedByteArray` can take less memory than `PackedInt32Array`, but `TypedArray<uint8_t>` and `TypedArray<int32_t>` will both take the same memory.

Common C# collection types such as `List<T>` or `T[]` work more like packed arrays in this sense, so I can see where the confusion may be coming from, but this is also why I think it's important to mention explicitly in the documentation that the elements are stored as `Variant` and not `T`. And all of this also applies to dictionaries.

Perhaps there's a better way to describe how these types work, but it should still be clear that the underlying type stored is `Variant` even if conceptually it feels like they store `T` elements.
